glosses: to abhor (to feel hatred and disgust for)
een afschuw hebben voor
iets slecht keuren
Abscheu gegen jemanden oder etwas empfinden

examples.text: Ich verabscheue diesen bestialischen Gestank.
Mörder werden verabscheut.
„Der Pater verabscheute die afrikanische Kultur und erwartete eine rigorose Assimilation seiner Missionszöglinge an westliche Werte.“

glosses: To dislike (someone or something) intensely; to loathe.

examples.text: I detest snakes.
Who dares think one thing, and another tell, / My heart detests him as the gates of hell.
Nurse Cramer had a cute nose and a radiant, blooming complexion dotted with fetching sprays of adorable freckles that Yossarian detested.

glosses: To witness against; to denounce; to condemn.

examples.text: The heresy of Nestorius […] was detested in the Eastern churches.
God hath detested them with his own mouth.

glosses: Abominable; detested.
To feel disgust towards; to loathe or detest thoroughly; to hate in the highest degree, as if with religious dread.

examples.text: "Much as I abominate writing, I would not give up Mr. Collins's correspondence for any consideration."

glosses: To dislike strongly.

examples.text: I absolutely abominate waking up early on weekends.

glosses: To regard (someone or something) as horrifying or detestable; to feel great repugnance toward.

examples.text: I absolutely abhor being stuck in traffic jams.
Let loue bee without dissimulation: abhorre that which is euill, cleaue to that which is good.

I have risked alienating some members with criticism of the war, reminding them, for example, that the Lord abhors our worship of the false gods of Western affluence, worldly power and high technology. I agree with Michael J. Easley, the senior pastor-teacher of Immanuel Bible Church in Springfield, when he says, "I think my 'job' is to clearly teach the Scriptures, not be persuaded by what may or may not be our people's views."

glosses: To fill with horror or disgust.

examples.text:
But neuer taynt my Loue. I cannot say Whore,
It do's abhorre me now I speake the word,
To do the Act, that might the addition earne,
Not the worlds Masse of vanitie could make me.

glosses: To turn aside or avoid; to keep away from; to reject.
To protest against; to reject solemnly.

examples.text:
I vtterly abhorre; yea, from my Soule
Refuse you for my Iudge, whom yet once more
I hold my most malicious Foe, and thinke not
At all a Friend to truth.

glosses: To feel horror, disgust, or dislike (towards); to be contrary or averse (to); construed with from.

examples.text: Also in those daunces were enterlased dities of wanton loue or ribaudry, with frequent remembrance of the moste vile idolis Venus and Bacchus, as it were that the daunce were to their honour and memorie, whiche most of all abhorred from Christes religion, sauerynge the auncient errour of paganysme.

Either then the law by harmless and needful dispenses, which the gospel is now made to deny, must have anticipated and exceeded the grace of the gospel, or else must be found to have given politic and superficial graces without real pardon, saying in general, “do this and live,” and yet deceiving and damning underhand with unsound and hollow permissions; which is utterly abhorring from the end of all law, as hath been shewed.

glosses: Differ entirely from.
To detest, hate, or revile (someone or something).

examples.text: I loathe scrubbing toilets.
I absolutely loathe this place.
Loathing the honeyed cakes, I long for bread.
To Scriptures read they muſt their leaſure frame, / Then loath they will both luſt and wanton love; […]
[…] O Hypocrites! ye hope for Enjoyment of Chriſt, but be perſwaded of it, Chriſt ſhall eternally loath you, and ye ſhall eternally loath Chriſt: […]
Quick-loving hearts, I thought, may quickly loathe

This movie is a historical achievement: Clint Eastwood, an icon of violence, has made us loathe violence as an obscenity. “Mystic River” hurts the way sad stories always hurt, but the craft and love with which it has been made transfigure pain into a moviegoer’s rapture

glosses: To induce or inspire disgust (in a person)

examples.text:
How heartily he serves me! his face loathes one,
But look upon his care, who would not love him?

glosses: Maudire.
Avoir en aversion ; réprouver.

examples.text: Oh ! Dieu merci, non ; cela m’est bien égal. Je hais profondément la huguenoterie, mais je ne déteste pas les huguenots, et puis c’est la mode.

Sa femme était morte, ses enfants le détestaient, une rebeue lui parlait comme à un chien, pour le Syndicat il était un traître, pour le gouvernement le dernier des cons, il ne serait pas ministre et sans doute plus député pour longtemps, qu'est-ce qui lui restait ?

glosses: Ne pas supporter ; ne pas aimer ; ne pas apprécier.

examples.text: Elle se console d’avoir oublié ses cigarettes, détestant de fumer dans le noir.
Au début, je le détestais avec sa fixette sur la mariologie, sa morale moyenâgeuse et ses prises de position rétrogrades sur la contraception. Et puis je suis tombée amoureuse de lui.
— […], et nous avons été ensemble boire une petite goutte au débit d’à côté ; le pauvre vieux ne déteste pas ça, quoi qu'il n'en ait jamais abusé.
Pyrrhon aimait que l’orateur Démosthène injuriât si bien Philippe; il n’eût pas détesté que Philippe injuriât aussi bien l’orateur Démosthène.

glosses: Sentir intenso rechazo hacia algo o alguien
Maldecir tomando el cielo por testigo.
Experimentar una profunda aversión por algo o alguien.

examples.text: Y viendo sus hermanos que su padre lo amaba más que a todos sus hermanos, aborrecíanle, y no le podían hablar pacíficamente.

glosses: Perder el gusto por algo en específico.

examples.text: Antes le gustaban los sesos, pero los aborreció
